title: SP-808 block diagram → firmware map
firmware_mapping: Stock SP8EXall.bin; runtime=file offset+0x100000. A6/v3 entries are explicitly identified.
scope: Maps known areas and gaps; not an exhaustive instruction/access census. Diagram wiring does not prove a software driver or memory address. No 400xxx implementation was disassembled.

nodes.name: CPU — IC7 HD6432653
nodes.observed: The diagram identifies IC7 as the H8S CPU. All listed routines execute H8 instructions; 100AB0 programs TPU0 and starts TSTR bit 0.
nodes.unresolved: TPU0's downstream physical role is not established. Do not equate it with clock-generator IC19 or infer a sample-rate selection from timing constants.

nodes.name: Application flash — IC9 LH28F800SUT
firmware: Stock SP ROM image: 100000–1C0003 in the corpus
nodes.observed: The diagram shows CPU-bus flash. The checked BIN holds H8 code, tables, strings and ESP records; its first instruction jumps to startup.
nodes.unresolved: The complete updater/flash-programming implementation is not established here. The first 32 bytes include executable entry code and metadata; do not subtract 0x20 from mapped firmware addresses.

nodes.name: CPU DRAM — IC8 TMS418169A
firmware: 12CC54: application RAM clear and initializer copy
registers: 401000: shared storage context; 5D0000: active storage buffer
nodes.observed: Firmware accesses and executes external DRAM addresses; diagram IC8 is connected to the CPU bus.
nodes.unresolved: Exact chip-select geometry/aliasing is not proven. The source that populates inherited 400xxx executable services is unresolved; it is not part of the supplied SP application BIN.
sources: Evidence Ledger §§32.1,38 and final programmed-vector clarification

nodes.name: I/F gate array — IC13 SLA919FF0J
nodes.observed: Diagram connects the gate array to Zip, LCD, switch/LED and audio-related paths. SP callers use opaque services; A6 accesses the ATA-like window directly.
nodes.unresolved: Only the storage-side interface has a concrete application mapping here. The gate array's LCD, panel and audio subinterfaces are not assigned undocumented register meanings.

nodes.name: Internal Zip drive
registers: 400380 / 4003A8 / 4003AC: opaque DRAM service entry addresses, not hardware registers
nodes.observed: Physical internal-bus traces contain A1 IDENTIFY PACKET, A0 PACKET, A8 READ(12), AA WRITE(12). Application read/write call chains correlate with the internal backend.
nodes.unresolved: Stock packet construction and transfer-engine code inside 400xxx remain unavailable. Do not assign the external IOMEGA/ZIP gate at 12AA14 to this drive path.
sources: Evidence Ledger historical ATAPI trace/formatter addendum

nodes.name: LCD unit
nodes.observed: UI records pass byte-sized geometry to drawing-like service calls. Diagram routes LCD through the gate array.
nodes.unresolved: Exact primitive names, LCD bus/register addresses, screen-coordinate conventions and controller protocol are unproven. High-level UI mapping does not identify low-level LCD writes.
sources: Fresh IDA: UI primitive caller; UI geometry

nodes.name: Panel and switch boards — switches / LEDs
firmware: 1258D8: diagnostic boot decision queries button codes through 1381BC
registers: 400494: group query; 1381BC tests a returned matrix bit
nodes.observed: 1381BC derives a group and bit from the lookup result, calls 400494, masks that bit and returns Boolean. Diagram switches/LEDs connect to the gate array.
nodes.unresolved: Individual physical-button labels, scan-register implementation and LED write paths have not been established by this map. Do not assume drawing functions scan inputs.
sources: Evidence Ledger Develop Monitor / Boot-mode dispatch

nodes.name: Panel faders
registers: Candidate H8 A/D interface: ADDRA/B/C/D FFFF90/92/94/96; ADCSR FFFF98; ADCR FFFF99
nodes.observed: The diagram draws the fader connection directly to the CPU.
nodes.unresolved: H8 ADC acquisition is plausible, but no fader-channel assignment or firmware acquisition path was recovered. Empty fixed-address IDA xrefs do not establish absence; loaded-pointer and inherited-service paths remain possible.
sources: IDA/H8.cfg register names only (not semantic proof)

nodes.name: Beam board / D-Beam
firmware: 12E626: consumes selected curve and processed input byte
nodes.observed: 12EAF0 multiplies two byte indices by 256, adds 1589D2 and stores two pointers. The documented callback records connect calibration to D BEAM SETUP / Auto Setup Sens?. Diagram links beam board to CPU.
nodes.unresolved: Physical input acquisition pins, ADC/timer assignment and IR emitter/detector control are not established. These are processed calibration curves, not DSP program records.

nodes.name: Pedal input
nodes.observed: Diagram shows the pedal signal entering the CPU.
nodes.unresolved: CPU port, electrical interpretation, debounce and application action mapping are untraced. A direct CPU wire does not establish an ADC input.

nodes.name: MIDI board
nodes.observed: Fresh 13C5C0 instructions read RDR0, poll SSR0 bit 7, write TDR0, clear SSR0 bit 7 and RTS through a saved successor. Independent firmware protocol evidence includes MIDI status, running status and SysEx parsing.
nodes.unresolved: Complete MIDI parser/ISR ownership remains incomplete. 13C5C0 is a forwarding/chaining hook, not evidence that this one routine implements all MIDI. SCI1/CN7 is a separate interface.
sources: Evidence Ledger SCI1 is distinct from MIDI

nodes.name: DSP — IC11 TC170C140AF (ESP)
registers: PRAM0 C00000; PRAM1 C01000; controls C02000–C02005
Type-1 ROM image 15E470–15E754; PRAM1 starts at index 03C
nodes.observed: 108A7E computes C00000/C01000 plus masked selector offset and writes the supplied longword; it maintains corresponding RAM shadows. Firmware diagnoses DEVICE(ESP). Diagram labels IC11 TC170C140AF. Later production corpus reconstruction finds 25 type images and 8,381 records.
nodes.unresolved: Register-to-IC11 correspondence is strongly supported, not individually traced on the bus here. Complete opcode timing, opcode 50 and 34/B0 details remain unresolved. Apply the later executable-ESP interpretation over older descriptor-only prose.

nodes.name: DSP DRAM — IC12 LH62800K
registers: ERAM exercised indirectly through ESP programs; no direct H8 base assigned
nodes.observed: The diagram connects IC12 to the DSP rather than directly to the CPU bus. Firmware has distinct indirect ERAM tests and address-field updates.
nodes.unresolved: ERAM-to-IC12 physical correspondence is plausible but unproven. Do not equate IC12 with the main CPU DRAM or assert which audio/sample buffers reside here.

nodes.name: Clock generator — IC19 TC9246F
firmware: No exact IC19 programming routine established
100A8C / 100AB0 are confirmed TPU0 programming, not an identified IC19 driver
nodes.observed: Diagram connects the CPU-side control path to the clock generator and its output toward audio hardware.
nodes.unresolved: Control pins/protocol and sample-clock selection are untraced. Values 850/880/870/860 at 1599D2 are timer parameters; their association with this chip or audio rates is not established.

nodes.name: Main-board A/D–D/A — IC23 / IC24 AK4520
firmware: ESP coefficient/effect code maps to processing, not an identified AK4520 control driver
nodes.observed: Diagram places two AK4520 converters on the audio path, with digital connections toward the gate-array/DSP side.
nodes.unresolved: Codec initialization, serial control, digital routing and converter-specific H8 writes have not been mapped. H8 ADDRA/ADCSR are MCU peripherals, not these audio codecs.

nodes.name: Analog input VR, output mute and phones selection
firmware: No exact IC35 mute or IC33/IC35 selection routine established
nodes.observed: Diagram shows input VR controls, MUTE IC35 4053 and SEL IC33/IC35 4053 paths to master, aux and phones outputs.
nodes.unresolved: Analog potentiometer paths do not imply H8-readable controls. CPU/ASIC control wiring, mute polarity and output-selection firmware require schematic/control-flow tracing.

nodes.name: Option-board SCSI — IC4 NCR53CF92
registers: IER/ISR bit 3; 426BF8 and subsequent transfer state
nodes.observed: 123864 clears ISR/IER bit 3 and reads/writes 800002–800006, advances buffer state and calls transfer helpers. Target-indexed firmware uses SCSI-style CDBs. Diagram puts an NCR53CF92 and separate Zip device on SP808-OP1.
nodes.unresolved: Exact register-to-chip bus decode and full 880000 transfer-hardware implementation are not newly proven here. The option-board Zip label is separate from the main-board internal Zip path.

nodes.name: Option-board digital I/O and extra D/A
nodes.observed: Diagram labels D.OUT I/F IC2 TC9271F, D.IN I/F IC3 LC8905V and D/A IC7/8/9 AK4324, with digital paths into the main board.
nodes.unresolved: Option detection, digital lock/status, clock-source selection and individual channel routing/control paths are not assigned routines. Do not map the SCSI driver to all option-board hardware merely because it shares a board.
